ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of rectangle $ABCD$ intersect at point $O$. $AE$ bisects $\angle BAD$ and intersects $BC$ at point $E$. Connect $OE$. If $OE \perp BC$ and $OE = 1$, what is the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, \\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\angle BAD=90^\circ$, $OA=OC$, $OB=OD$, $AC=BD$, \\
$\therefore OB=OC$, \\
Since $OE\perp BC$, \\
$\therefore BE=CE$, \\
$\therefore OE$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, \\
$\therefore AB=2OE=2$, \\
Since $AE$ bisects $\angle BAD$, \\
$\therefore \angle BAE=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \triangle ABE$ is an isosceles right triangle, \\
$\therefore BE=AB=2$, \\
$\therefore BC=2BE=4$, \\
$\therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^{2}+BC^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}+4^{2}}=\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangle ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right; diagonals AC and BD intersect at point O; point E is on the bottom side BC, segment OE goes vertically from O to E, and is marked as perpendicular to BC; segment AE is also drawn from A to E, indicating that AE bisects the right angle BAD. Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rectangle, the two diagonals bisect each other and are equal, so O is the midpoint of AC and BD, and OB = OC. Also because OE is perpendicular to BC, triangles OBE and OCE are both right triangles; they share the right-angle side OE, and the hypotenuses OB = OC, so it can be obtained that BE = CE, that is, E is the midpoint of BC. Thus, in triangle ABC, O is the midpoint of AC and E is the midpoint of BC, so OE is the midline of triangle ABC, OE is parallel to AB, and OE = AB/2. Given OE = 1, so AB = 2. Since AE bisects angle BAD, and angle BAD = 90°, angle BAE = 45°. Also AB is perpendicular to BE, so triangle ABE is an isosceles right triangle, BE = AB = 2. Because E is the midpoint of BC, BC = 2BE = 4. Finally, in right triangle ABC, AC = sqrt(AB^2 + BC^2) = sqrt(2^2 + 4^2) = sqrt(20) = 2sqrt(5).
